title: Paris, 1893
hookLine: he dies in a Paris hotel, far from home

lines: A MAN WEAK AFTER A STROKE.
A CITY THAT WAS NEVER HOME.
cards: A hotel room in Paris. Outside, the boulevards, the cafés, the noise of a great city. Inside, a man lies weak after a stroke, his body failing.
He was born in Lahore. He sat on a throne as a child, lost it, grew up in a garden by the Ganges, lived as a gentleman in Suffolk, and came back to Sikhi in a port at Aden.
Now he is here, in a rented room in a city that was never his home.

teach.b: After Aden, Duleep Singh could not go to India and would not go back to his old life in England. He went to Paris. He tried to win support abroad for his claim to the Punjab, and even traveled to Russia hoping for help.
None came. His money ran low, his first wife died, and his health broke.

Late in life, weakened, he wrote to Queen Victoria asking her pardon, and she forgave him. They met once more: the Queen who held his diamond, and the Maharaja who had once fought her government with words.

teach.h: A DEATH IN PARIS, A GRAVE IN SUFFOLK.
teach.b: He died in a hotel in Paris, far from the Punjab and far from Elveden. His body was taken back to England and buried in the churchyard at Elveden, beside his wife and son, with a Christian service.
He had come back to Sikhi, but he was not cremated with Sikh rites. For some who tell his story, that is one more thing taken from him.
In a hymn of Guru Arjan, the Guru says that since he found the company of the holy, he has forgotten all envy of others; no one is his enemy and no one is a stranger, and he gets along with everyone.
An exile is someone everywhere treats as a stranger. The Guru's line describes a company where nobody is one. So today's line reaches past Duleep Singh, to everyone far from home.

how: Duleep Singh is buried at Elveden in Suffolk, and Sikh visitors to the churchyard remember him there; some Sikhs hold prayers for him and his mother at gatherings about the end of the kingdom.

games.q: you're Duleep Singh, weak and short of money in Paris. your claim to the Punjab has gone nowhere. what do you do, as the histories tell it?
o: make one more attempt to reach India.
write to Queen Victoria asking her pardon.
go back to live at Elveden.
games.why: he asked her pardon and she forgave him; he died in Paris, and was buried at Elveden.

practice: Bring to mind people living somewhere that isn't home: refugees, migrants, students abroad, a neighbor who arrived last year, someone in a hospital or a prison.
You don't need faces or names; just hold them all in your mind for a while, without judging how they got there. If you pray, you can hold them before God, and say Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Paris. The city where Duleep Singh, the boy king of the Punjab, died in a hotel room, far from the land he was born to rule. Today's word.

orig.note: bigana, a stranger; Guru Arjan's hymn says no one is an enemy and no one is a stranger.

carryVoice: Your line: for all exiles. In the Guru's company, nobody is a stranger. Nine hundred forty-six days, and counting.
